title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ يحاضر عن مفهوم التغيير في الاسلام آلياته و ضوابطه
title_en: The Sheikh Lectures on the Concept of Change in Islam: Its Mechanisms and What Governs It
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله تعالى يوم الخميس 29 – 01- 2015م محاضرة بعنوان : " مفهوم التغيير في الإسلام: آلياته وضوابطه" ضمن فعاليات اليوم الأول من المؤتمر العام الثاني عشر للندوة العالمية للشباب الإسلامي المنعقد بمدينة مراكش المغربية ؛ و قد تحدث فضيلة الشيخ عن آليات التغيير في الإسلام مشددا على مجموعة من الضوابط التي يجب توفرها ؛ مبينا أن التغيير يكون إيجابيا كما يكون سلبيا و هذه سنة كونية و العالم من حولنا متغير ، فالزيادة في الخير تغيير إيجابي كما الزيادة في الشر تغيير سلبي و التغيير المطلوب هو التغيير الإيجابي النافع " إن الله لا يغير ما بقوم حتى يغيروا ما بأنفسهم " . لمشاهدة المحاضرة كاملة اضغط هنا
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew (may God the Exalted preserve him) delivered on Thursday 29-01-2015 a lecture entitled 'The Concept of Change in Islam: Its Mechanisms and What Governs It', as part of the proceedings of the first day of the twelfth general conference of the World Assembly of Muslim Youth, held in the Moroccan city of Marrakesh.

The Sheikh spoke of the mechanisms of change in Islam, pressing a set of governing conditions that must be met; explaining that change may be positive and may be negative, and that this is a pattern God has set in creation, the world around us being in change. An increase in good is a positive change, just as an increase in evil is a negative change; and the change that is called for is the positive, beneficial change — {God does not change what is with a people until they change what is in themselves} (Sūrat al-Raʿd 13:11).

a number of constraints that have to be in place
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The report says the Sheikh stressed a set of governing conditions for change and then does not state a single one of them. The record therefore carries the topic of the lecture and none of its substance, and must not be displayed as though it set out his position on how change may legitimately be pursued. The full lecture was behind a link the record no longer resolves.

flags.context: و هذه سنة كونية و العالم من حولنا متغير

a law of the created order
flags.note: سنن كونية are the regularities God has established in creation, as distinct from the سنن شرعية of revealed law. 'Natural law' would be wrong, importing a different tradition. Not in the project glossary; a candidate for addition.

flags.note: SOURCE FORMATTING. The source puts it in ordinary quotation marks with no reference, the same marks it uses elsewhere for prophetic reports; it is Qur'anic. The English uses curly braces and supplies the reference. Whoever cleans the corpus globally should note that quotation marks in body_ar do not distinguish scripture from hadith.
